extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in democracy, social critique, and 19th-century literature
extracted.subtask_description: A 19th-century literary and political essay addressing democracy, social economy, literature, and education; mixes prescriptive social standards with cultural criticism. The text offers normative claims about what constitutes a healthy democracy, good literature, and proper schooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance acknowledgment of society's faults and values
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us, not ignoring the dross, give fit stress to these precious immortal values also.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While recognizing what is dismal and noisome in current society, explicitly emphasize the inexhaustible supplies of general humanity and the positive, immortal values that justify faith and hope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy as people's government and moral test
rubrics_metrics.description: Only here in America ... has at last arisen, and now stands, what never before took positive form and sway, the People ... the stablest, solidest-based government of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the nation by the presence and development of 'the People' en masse; view democratic institutions as both established and tested, strengthened by trials of war and peace, and as bearing a moral responsibility to improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of the Poverty Question / social-economic organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneath the whole political world... what most presses and perplexes to-day ... is of social and economic organization, the treatment of working-people by employers ... the Poverty Question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat questions of progress, finance, tariffs, and strength as evolving from how society treats working people; place the welfare and conditions of labor at the core of political and social evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate wealth with moral health
rubrics_metrics.description: The wealth of the civilized world... as contrasted with its poverty -- what does it derivatively stand for ... the wealth of to-day mainly results from rapine, murder, outrages ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing prosperity, consider historical and moral sources of wealth; recognize that ostensible wealth may be tainted and not a reliable sign of a healthy society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and virtue often found among the poor
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in what are call'd the poorest, lowest characters you will sometimes, nay generally, find glints of the most sublime virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dismissing lower classes as morally inferior; include their potential for heroism and virtue when judging the social fabric and prospects for the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure national success by condition of the masses (homesteads/land ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true prosperity of a nation is not in the great wealth of a special class, but is only to be really attain'd in having the bulk of the people provided with homes or land in fee simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess economic policy (e.g., protection) by asking 'into whose pockets does this plunder really go?' and favor distributional outcomes that give secure property and independence to the many.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the widest general suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: As to general suffrage... the more general it is, the better. I favor the widest opening of the doors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote broad electoral inclusion; view widened franchise as a safeguard and ventilator for democracy rather than a threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections express majority will rather than guarantee exceptional genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Those offices... are, indeed, at best, the mere business agencies of the people... We elect Presidents, Congressmen, &c., not so much to have them consider and decide for us, but as surest practical means of expressing the will of majorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the practical, representative function of electoral offices and avoid evaluating them solely by whether they attract first-class geniuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy requires moral, spiritual, and esthetic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Soon, it will be fully realized that ostensible wealth and money-making ... imperatively necessitate something beyond--namely, the sane, eternal moral and spiritual-esthetic attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the health and future of the State by whether moral, spiritual, and aesthetic qualities permeate society; economic success alone is insufficient for flourishing democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: National literature must transform inherited legacies into an American physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: What we have to do to-day is to receive them cheerfully, and to give them ensemble, and a modern American and democratic physiognomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating or assessing American literature, aim to synthesize global cultural legacies into a distinctively American expression rather than merely imitating foreign models.

rubrics_metrics.name: True literature comprises a small class of primal works vs. many derivative ones
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain purposes... the first consisting of only a score or two... Then the second class, books and writings innumerable, incessant... The works of the first class... have their own laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish seminal, law-making works from the multitude of offshoots; do not conflate high quantity of print with genuine literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom defined as license under the law
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom only opens entire activity and license under the law... We only attain to freedom by a knowledge of, and implicit obedience to, Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptualize and evaluate liberty as compatible with and realized through obedience to universal/eternal laws; reject the notion that freedom means escape from any law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal culmination measured by broad-based comfort and land ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The final culmination... will be the production and perennial establishment of millions of comfortable city homesteads and moderate-sized farms, healthy and independent, single separate ownership, fee simple, life in them complete but cheap, within reach of all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the widespread ownership of comfortable homes and moderate farms as the yardstick of democratic success; exceptional concentrated wealth is suspect except insofar as it contributes to this end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal of political leadership emerging from the masses
rubrics_metrics.description: I say no body of men are fit to make Presidents, Judges, and Generals, unless they themselves supply the best specimens of the same... I would be much pleas'd to see some heroic... American blacksmith or boatman... walk into the Presidency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value practical, working-class qualifications and character as appropriate sources for high public office; endorse leaders whose experience connects them to ordinary life and labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve polyglot, pluralist national character
rubrics_metrics.description: I like well our polyglot construction-stamp... All nations here--a home for every race on earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote and evaluate national institutions by their tolerance, retention, and accommodation of multiple languages, cultures, and immigrant communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should reject corporal punishment and favor gentleness
rubrics_metrics.description: Happily a worthier and more philosophical system is proving to men that schools can be better govern'd than by lashes and tears... May propitious gales speed that day!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge school governance and teachers by humane methods; condemn brutal, punitive masters and prefer pedagogies that use kindness and restraint rather than rods and lashings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine association commitments with individual freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the problems presented... is, how to combine one's duty and policy as a member of associations... with essential freedom as an individual personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess civic life and personal development by the ability to maintain membership and duty within groups while preserving independent thought, action, and self-development.
